reasoning.text: Reference class: I anchor on the October-to-November change base rate for the same NSA CPS occupation series, because the target is a level series and the seasonal transition from October to November is more relevant than the full-month average change. I retained the 2018-2024 sample because those were the complete October-November pairs explicitly extracted into the captured arithmetic; I did not add 2016-2017 during review because their paired values were not in the draft's captured calculation evidence.

Prior/update/interval: persistence prior is October 2026 at 5.757 million; historical sample is same-series October-to-November changes from 2018-2024 with 2025 omitted because October was unavailable; adjustment components are +0.0329 million seasonal base-rate change and no extra policy or one-off adjustment; I do not fit a fuller trend model because recent same-series changes average only +0.0108 million while CPS occupation-cell noise is about 0.10 million at this horizon; interval method uses the month-specific change dispersion, sigma = 0.1086 million, so 1.28*sigma = 0.1390 million; final implied bounds are 5.7899 - 0.1390 = 5.6509 and 5.7899 + 0.1390 = 5.9289 million.

Upside risk is a broad CPS rebound or unusually strong healthcare support hiring like the large positive October-to-November moves in 2020 or 2024 that would land above the interval, roughly above 5.929 million. Downside risk is sampling noise or a November pullback similar to 2023 that would land below the interval, roughly below 5.651 million. Outside the interval would most likely reflect CPS sampling volatility in this small occupation cell rather than a true monthly structural break.
